title: Generic provisional DLMS analysis bundle

rules.title: Expected workbook sheet coverage
rules.why: Confirms the submitted report contains the expected BCS workbook structure.
rules.limitation: A complete sheet count does not prove each table is compatible.
rules.followUp: Review missing-sheet list and adapter mapping.

rules.title: Mandatory sheet availability
rules.why: Meter configuration, self-diagnostics, and instantaneous data are mandatory for this adapter.
rules.limitation: This is an input-quality gate, not a device diagnosis.
rules.followUp: Upload a complete compatible report.

rules.title: Profile source availability
rules.why: Profile evidence is needed for interval and consumption checks.
rules.limitation: A missing profile does not prove a meter fault.
rules.followUp: Obtain a report with at least one load or billing profile.

rules.title: Event source availability
rules.why: Event history is required to assess contextual electrical stress and time-based anomalies.
rules.limitation: Empty event sheets can be valid; this only checks whether event sources exist.
rules.followUp: Check adapter coverage or retrieve an event-enabled report.

rules.title: Meter serial extraction
rules.why: A technical report must expose a canonical meter serial before it can be attached to a case.
rules.limitation: This finding does not decide which FFR case owns the data.
rules.followUp: Configure the identity locator or obtain a supported report.

rules.title: Configuration content
rules.why: Basic configuration values support model-aware thresholds and evidence traceability.
rules.limitation: Configuration completeness is not a functional health test.
rules.followUp: Check the MeterConfiguration export.

rules.title: Meter model captured
rules.why: Model and variant data allow future model-specific profiles to supersede generic limits.
rules.limitation: Generic provisional limits may still be used when the model is absent.
rules.followUp: Map the model field in adapter settings.

rules.title: Voltage reference available
rules.why: Rated voltage should ideally come from meter configuration instead of a generic profile.
rules.limitation: The provisional fallback remains clearly identified when this value is absent.
rules.followUp: Configure rated-voltage mapping for this model.

rules.title: Current reference available
rules.why: Rated current enables model-aware current plausibility checks.
rules.limitation: No current-overload conclusion is made without a configured rating.
rules.followUp: Configure rated-current mapping for this model.

rules.title: Units or scalers present
rules.why: Units and scalers reduce the risk of treating a mapped value as a physical reading.
rules.limitation: Presence alone does not validate every scaler.
rules.followUp: Review units/scalers in adapter settings.

rules.title: Self-diagnostic data available
rules.why: Self-diagnostic flags are a primary source for display, battery, and health context.
rules.limitation: A present flag is not a component-level diagnosis.
rules.followUp: Retrieve the SelfDiagnostic sheet.

rules.title: Instantaneous data available
rules.why: Instantaneous readings provide the current electrical reference point.
rules.limitation: One instantaneous reading is not a historical trend.
rules.followUp: Retrieve the IP sheet.

rules.title: Block-load records available
rules.why: Checks that a populated block-load profile was found.
rules.limitation: Record presence does not prove the profile is complete.
rules.followUp: Retrieve the block-load profile.

rules.title: Profile timestamp parsing
rules.why: Checks timestamps before interval and chronology calculations are trusted.
rules.limitation: Only detected profile rows are evaluated.
rules.followUp: Review date/time format in the adapter.

rules.title: Profile interval determined
rules.why: A known interval is required to assess gaps and expected data density.
rules.limitation: Fallback interval is not substituted as observed evidence.
rules.followUp: Confirm interval mapping for this model.

rules.title: Duplicate profile intervals
rules.why: Duplicate records can distort energy and trend calculations.
rules.limitation: This does not identify why a duplicate exists.
rules.followUp: Review raw profile export.

rules.title: Out-of-order profile intervals
rules.why: Chronological ordering is required for interval-based evidence.
rules.limitation: Ordering may be an export artifact.
rules.followUp: Review source ordering and adapter settings.

rules.title: Long profile gaps
rules.why: A long interval gap weakens any conclusion that relies on continuous history.
rules.limitation: A gap does not establish a communication or meter fault.
rules.followUp: Obtain the missing period or validate data retrieval.

rules.title: Profile window completeness
rules.why: Trend-dependent checks need a sufficient time window.
rules.limitation: Short windows are valid evidence but have limited diagnostic depth.
rules.followUp: Retrieve a longer period when trend analysis is needed.

rules.title: Profile voltage data available
rules.why: Voltage distribution requires a recognizable profile voltage column.
rules.limitation: Instantaneous voltage is still evaluated separately.
rules.followUp: Map the profile voltage column.

rules.title: Low profile voltage excursion
rules.why: Flags a profile voltage value outside the provisional critical range.
rules.limitation: It supports electrical-stress investigation, not a component cause.
rules.followUp: Verify voltage source, nominal rating, and event history.

rules.title: High profile voltage excursion
rules.why: Flags a profile voltage maximum outside the provisional critical range.
rules.limitation: The underlying source and duration must be reviewed.
rules.followUp: Verify voltage source, nominal rating, and event history.

rules.title: Profile median voltage
rules.why: Flags sustained median voltage outside the provisional warning range.
rules.limitation: Does not prove supply origin or damage mechanism.
rules.followUp: Compare with configuration and available event history.

rules.title: Zero-voltage profile periods
rules.why: Identifies zero-valued voltage intervals that may need correlation with power events.
rules.limitation: Zero can be a valid outage or mapping condition.
rules.followUp: Correlate with power-failure events and raw records.

rules.title: Profile current data available
rules.why: Current distribution supports abnormal-reading and loading context.
rules.limitation: Current alone does not determine accuracy.
rules.followUp: Map the profile current column.

rules.title: Zero-current profile periods
rules.why: Identifies zero-current periods for context.
rules.limitation: Zero current can be normal for no-load periods.
rules.followUp: Compare with voltage, load, and event context.

rules.title: Import register monotonicity
rules.why: Checks whether mapped import energy decreases between readings.
rules.limitation: Scaler or column mapping errors can mimic a physical anomaly.
rules.followUp: Validate register mapping and scaler before interpretation.

rules.title: Export register monotonicity
rules.why: Checks whether mapped export energy decreases between readings.
rules.limitation: Scaler or column mapping errors can mimic a physical anomaly.
rules.followUp: Validate register mapping and scaler before interpretation.

rules.title: Repeated profile values
rules.why: Flags a long repeated numeric run that could be an export or mapping signal.
rules.limitation: A repeated value is not automatically an impossible physical reading.
rules.followUp: Review raw records and meter behavior.

rules.title: Profile versus register consistency
rules.why: Signals that comparable profile/register fields were not available for reconciliation.
rules.limitation: This is a coverage gap rather than an anomaly.
rules.followUp: Configure compatible profile and register fields.

rules.title: Voltage-event source available
rules.why: Voltage-event history supports electrical-stress context.
rules.limitation: No event source does not prove no events occurred.
rules.followUp: Confirm voltage event export.

rules.title: Power-event source available
rules.why: Power-event history supports outage and restoration context.
rules.limitation: No event source does not prove no events occurred.
rules.followUp: Confirm power event export.

rules.title: Recurring overvoltage events
rules.why: Repeated overvoltage records provide provisional electrical-stress context.
rules.limitation: Event count does not identify a failed component or origin.
rules.followUp: Review event timestamps, voltage profile, and physical evidence.

rules.title: Recurring undervoltage events
rules.why: Repeated undervoltage records provide supply-quality context.
rules.limitation: This is not proof of a meter internal failure.
rules.followUp: Review event timestamps and supply conditions.

rules.title: Recurring power-failure events
rules.why: Repeated power-failure records provide outage and stress context.
rules.limitation: Counts alone do not establish whether a device or grid condition initiated the event.
rules.followUp: Review occurrence/restoration sequence.

rules.title: Recurring current-reversal events
rules.why: Repeated current-reversal events provide tamper or wiring context.
rules.limitation: They do not prove tampering or liability.
rules.followUp: Validate event detail and field wiring evidence.

rules.title: Recurring low-PF events
rules.why: Repeated low-PF events can support a load-quality investigation.
rules.limitation: Low PF is only interpretable with sufficient load context.
rules.followUp: Check active power and load conditions.

rules.title: Event occurrence/restoration pairing
rules.why: Unpaired event transitions weaken duration and chronology interpretation.
rules.limitation: Not every vendor format exposes occurrence/restoration labels.
rules.followUp: Review source event format or configure pairing columns.

rules.title: Event chronology available
rules.why: Time evidence is needed to relate events to the reported complaint period.
rules.limitation: A timestamp count alone does not establish defect chronology.
rules.followUp: Configure event timestamp mapping.

rules.title: RTC transaction pattern
rules.why: Repeated RTC transactions can support an RTC-history investigation.
rules.limitation: It does not quantify clock drift by itself.
rules.followUp: Compare meter RTC against retrieval time and configuration.

rules.title: Programming transaction evidence
rules.why: Programming history is contextual evidence for configuration-related investigations.
rules.limitation: A cumulative count is not a fault without a baseline.
rules.followUp: Establish a baseline or compare sequential reports.

rules.title: Connect/disconnect history
rules.why: Connect/disconnect events are contextual evidence for output and communication complaints.
rules.limitation: Absence may reflect adapter mapping rather than device behavior.
rules.followUp: Map control-event values for this model.

rules.title: Load-limit history
rules.why: Load-limit events provide context for output and billing investigations.
rules.limitation: This does not confirm relay operation.
rules.followUp: Map load-limit event values for this model.

rules.title: Tamper-event context
rules.why: Detected tamper-labelled records provide a traceable context signal.
rules.limitation: A label does not establish intent or liability.
rules.followUp: Review the individual tamper event records.

rules.title: Electrical-stress event pattern
rules.why: Combines recurrent electrical-event counts into provisional context for physical and availability complaints.
rules.limitation: It cannot determine a burn location, physical damage, or root cause.
rules.followUp: Review electrical events with physical inspection evidence.

rules.title: Self-diagnostic health flag
rules.why: Uses the meter's exported overall diagnostic flag as provisional health context.
rules.limitation: An overall status does not identify a component-level cause.
rules.followUp: Review individual diagnostic flags and physical evidence.

rules.title: RTC battery diagnostic
rules.why: A failed RTC battery flag supports an RTC or power-domain investigation.
rules.limitation: It is not a confirmation of the observed complaint.
rules.followUp: Validate with direct RTC and battery test.

rules.title: Main battery diagnostic
rules.why: A failed main-battery flag supports a display or availability investigation.
rules.limitation: It cannot confirm display hardware or a failed component.
rules.followUp: Inspect display/supply condition and perform direct validation.

rules.title: Instantaneous voltage outside warning band
rules.why: Compares the instantaneous voltage to the editable provisional warning band.
rules.limitation: One reading is not a sustained supply-quality conclusion.
rules.followUp: Compare with profile distribution and voltage events.

rules.title: Instantaneous current zero
rules.why: Records zero current as contextual evidence for load and availability investigations.
rules.limitation: Zero current can be normal at no load.
rules.followUp: Compare with voltage and service/load context.

rules.title: Low PF at meaningful load
rules.why: Assesses PF only when the available active-power reading meets the editable minimum.
rules.limitation: Requires compatible active-power mapping; it is not an accuracy conclusion.
rules.followUp: Review load and power measurements.

rules.title: Display / no-display electrical context
rules.why: Uses existing diagnostic evidence to prioritize a display/power-domain inspection.
rules.limitation: DLMS cannot observe display pixels, backlight, or button mechanics.
rules.followUp: Inspect the display and supply region.

rules.title: Meter-dead electrical context
rules.why: Combines poor diagnostic status with zero current as a provisional availability signal.
rules.limitation: It cannot prove a dead meter without direct communication and physical tests.
rules.followUp: Perform direct communication and supply validation.

rules.title: Communication contextual coverage
rules.why: Makes explicit when a meter DLMS report lacks direct communications/heartbeat evidence.
rules.limitation: Meter DLMS is contextual only for NIC/Gateway communication health.
rules.followUp: Upload the NIC/Gateway communication report or validate manually.

rules.title: Abnormal-reading contextual coverage
rules.why: Makes visible whether the report contains enough compatible energy data for jump analysis.
rules.limitation: No conclusion is made if the required energy series is absent.
rules.followUp: Map energy registers and profile increments.

rules.title: Accuracy voltage context
rules.why: Flags a voltage reading outside the editable preliminary range.
rules.limitation: This is not a calibrated accuracy test.
rules.followUp: Validate with a traceable reference instrument.

rules.title: RTC drift measurement coverage
rules.why: Shows whether source timestamps support a drift calculation.
rules.limitation: RTC event count is not a drift measurement.
rules.followUp: Provide meter and retrieval timestamps with a defined reference period.

rules.title: Tamper contextual finding
rules.why: Uses recurrent reversal events as traceable tamper/wiring context.
rules.limitation: This does not determine intent, mechanism, or liability.
rules.followUp: Review detailed event and field inspection evidence.

rules.title: Output / relay contextual coverage
rules.why: Shows whether the current report can provide load-limit or output context.
rules.limitation: DLMS cannot prove a relay mechanical condition from this evidence alone.
rules.followUp: Map relay/load-limit events and perform manual test.

rules.title: Burnt or physical-damage electrical context
rules.why: Uses recurring electrical events to prioritize inspection for a reported burnt or damaged device.
rules.limitation: DLMS cannot locate a burn, confirm physical damage, or identify root cause.
rules.followUp: Inspect terminal/body/PCB evidence and validate manually.

summary: 60 configurable, source-linked DLMS checks. Findings are provisional and require review.
limitation: No rule in this bundle creates an approved RCA/CAPA or proves a component-level root cause.
